title: Repair F2: provenance-preserving source/projection split in the packet
description:
Repair dispatch for PR #543 review finding **F2** (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020
W10). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12` — its notes carry the review
and the integrating agent's verification. This is a MATERIAL change: it alters
the semantic shape of what the DM receives.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.8`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.8`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies installed. Touch nothing outside it.

Sibling dispatches own F1 (`signals.ts` + the capability preflight) and F3/F4/F5
(`orchestrator.ts`, the v2 reader, `measurements.ts`). Stay out of those.

## The defect

`packet.ts:packetCandidate()` sets `sourceProse: { data: object(record.data) }`
— the ENTIRE record body. `packetMessage.ts` then sends every string-valued
leaf to `### Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)` and every non-string leaf
to `### Typed projection`. **A primitive-type split is not a provenance
boundary.**

Verified failure, real pack, `spell:fireball`:
`data.mechanics.saves[0]` is `{ability: 'dexterity', damageOnSuccess: 'half'}`.
Both are importer-derived typed projection values. Both are strings. Both are
therefore presented to the DM under "verbatim; authoritative". The same class
covers typed string arrays, enum-like fields, and dice/damage strings, while a
mixed-type projection object is split across BOTH headings.

ADR 0020 and design section 7.2 require source prose and typed projections to
stay distinct, and forbid a projection from carrying source authority.

## Constraints on the fix

- **No field-name allow/deny list.** A growing list of leaf names
  (`ability`, `dice`, `damageOnSuccess`, …) is not a provenance boundary either
  and is explicitly rejected by the review.
- **Verified constraint:** `RulesRecord.data` is typed `unknown` and the pack
  carries NO per-field provenance (`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts:127`). You
  cannot read an existing boundary. W10 must ESTABLISH one and state it.
- **The producer owns it, not the renderer.** `PacketCandidate` must carry the
  distinction so it is durable in the evidence and measurable, rather than
  re-guessed at render time. Changing the packet shape is in scope and expected.

## The decided approach

The rules-pack compiler emits its derived material into declared projection
CONTAINERS; everything else in a record body is source-extracted. Establish
that boundary once, explicitly, and apply it RECURSIVELY by path:

- Declare the projection containers in ONE named constant with a comment
  explaining that this is W10's stated boundary, that the pack declares no
  per-field provenance of its own, and that the constant is a container rule
  and not a leaf-name list. The containers present in the corpus are
  `mechanics`, `upcast` and `executionReadiness` — VERIFY that against the pack
  before you rely on it, and say in your notes what you actually found.
- The rule is positional, not top-level-only: at any depth, a key that names a
  projection container makes everything beneath it projection. This is what
  makes `creature:adult-black-dragon` `data.actions[5]` split correctly —
  `actions[5].text` is source prose, `actions[5].mechanics` is projection.
- Everything not under a projection container is source material.
- **Residue is disclosed, not guessed.** If the walk meets a shape the rule
  cannot classify, it is reported in band rather than silently assigned. Do not
  invent a third silent default.

`data.mechanics.scaling.sourceText` quotes source text from INSIDE a
projection. It stays under projection — its value is still rendered verbatim,
correctly labelled as the projection's record of what it derived from. Do not
special-case it out; special-casing it is the beginning of the leaf-name list
the review forbids. Note the decision in the doc comment.

## What to change

1. `PacketCandidate` (in `discovery/types.ts`) splits the single `sourceProse`
   field into the source material and the typed projection, each keyed by JSON
   pointer path so the renderer emits paths without re-deriving them. Keep the
   shapes serializable — this goes through SQLite in the durable evidence.
2. `packet.ts` performs the split once, in `packetCandidate()`.
3. `packetMessage.ts` renders from the split instead of type-sniffing:
   `### Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)` gets source material only, and
   every projection value — string, number, array, object, null — goes under
   `### Typed projection (does not replace the source prose above)`.
4. Anything that reads `sourceProse` must follow. Check at minimum
   `measurements.ts` M9 (`exactSubstring` / `typedPath` matching) and M8's
   attribution check, plus the v2 reader in `shadow.ts` if the packet shape it
   admits changes. **M9 must still find a fixture's field-9 substrings** —
   several target prose, and at least one (`P8`'s
   `/data/mechanics/economies/use`) targets a TYPED path. Both must keep
   working; if M9 needs to search both halves, that is correct and expected.

## Evidence required

Extend `packetMessage.test.ts`, and the probe suites if the packet shape moves.
Use REAL records through the offline harness, never hand-authored packets.

- **P4 `spell:fireball`** — `ability: "dexterity"` and `damageOnSuccess: "half"`
  appear under the projection heading and NOT under the source heading; the
  description prose still appears verbatim under source, including
  "a 20-foot-radius sphere".
- **P3 `creature:adult-black-dragon`** — the mixed-type case:
  `data.actions[5].text` under source with its success-branch sentence intact,
  `data.actions[5].mechanics` entirely under projection, proving the rule is
  positional rather than top-level.
- **P10** — as the review names it; assert whichever of its prose and typed
  fields actually exist, and report what you found.
- Typed NUMERIC, ARRAY and NULL-valued projection fields each remain under
  projection (a type-based rule would have scattered these).
- No string-valued projection leaf appears anywhere under the source heading —
  assert this generically over every retained candidate of at least one probe,
  not just for the named fields, so a newly added projection string cannot
  regress silently.
- M9 still reports zero missing facts for every probe that reported zero
  before, including P8's typed-path fact. Run the existing probe suites.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape an existing test to make this pass. Tests
  that encode the old string-split behaviour SHOULD change — name each one and
  why in your notes.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the
  design document.
- House style: read the doc comments in `discovery/types.ts`, `packet.ts` and
  `shadow.ts` and match them. Every non-obvious shape says WHY it has that form
  and what wrong thing it makes unrepresentable.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
  times out at 10s under full-suite load. Pre-existing, filed, unrelated.
  Confirm with `npx vitest run packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts`, note it, do not
  fix it.
notes:
REPAIR DONE at commit 029006a on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.12.8 (parent 38f0a0c). npm run verify:worktree clean: format/check/typecheck clean, tests 5341 passed / 20 skipped (baseline at 38f0a0c was 5336/20; +5 = the 5 new evidence cases). packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts "packs publishable tarballs" (pre-existing filed flake) confirmed passing standalone (15/15), not touched.

CONTAINER SET VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL PACK (records.json, 1812 records) — did not take the spec's 3-name list on faith:
- mechanics (2268 occurrences): top-level on spell/feat/feature/condition/hazard/magic-item/action/stat-block, AND nested 3 levels deep inside creature actions/legendaryActions/reactions entries. Spec-named.
- upcast (92): always top-level, spell only. Spec-named.
- executionReadiness (240): always top-level, magic-item only. Spec-named.
- projection (22): always top-level, table records only (kindSchemas.ts table-projection validators: beastShapeOptions, destroyUndead, trade-goods/service-price rows). NOT named by the spec/review — found during verification, structurally identical to mechanics (kind-discriminated importer-computed object), so I ADDED it: omitting it would have left every table's derived rows misclassified as source prose, repeating the exact defect class this bead fixes.
- useProfile (35): always top-level, equipment only (consumption kind, clause ids, owner attribution). Also NOT named by the spec — also added. It even carries its own quoted source phrases (clauses[].sourcePhrase) exactly like mechanics.scaling.sourceText does, so the "container can quote its own source text" rule applies to it identically.
Final set: mechanics, upcast, executionReadiness, projection, useProfile — declared once in PROJECTION_CONTAINER_KEYS (packet.ts), with the full verification writeup in that constant's doc comment. Checked all 108 distinct top-level `data` keys in the corpus; nothing else shares this shape (armorClass/hitPoints/abilityScores/speed etc. are the compiler's direct stat-block transcription, not an omission-risk interpretation).

RECORD SHAPES THE WALK COULD NOT CLASSIFY: none found in the real pack — every record body is plain parsed JSON (string/number/boolean/null/array/plain-object), so `residue` is empty for every real candidate today. The residue mechanism (RecordDataResidue: {pointer, shape}) exists defensively because RulesRecord.data is typed `unknown` (a function, symbol, bigint, or non-plain object like Date/Map would be reported there instead of silently landing on either side); I did NOT add a synthetic/hand-authored unit test exercising that path — the file's established convention (packetMessage.test.ts, campaignRuleConsumption.test.ts) is real-record-only, hand-authoring a full DiscoveryCandidate/RetentionTrace just to hit dead code felt like it violated that convention and the "never hand-authored packets" instruction's spirit for a path the corpus cannot reach. Filing a low-priority follow-up for this.

EXISTING TESTS CHANGED, and why (none weakened — same assertions, corrected field/target per the new split):
- campaignRuleConsumption.test.ts:212-213 — `candidate?.sourceProse` -> `sourceMaterial`. "8d6" is still found because it's literally in Fireball's description prose ("A target takes 8d6 fire damage..."), not because of the projection value — added a comment explaining why this specific substring survives the rename unchanged.
- shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts:1725 — the cursed-attunement-addon regression test asserted the injected curse text via `sourceProse`; the curse is injected under `data.mechanics.curse` (a declared projection container: cursedAttunementAddon.ts), so it now asserts against `projection` instead. This is a genuine reclassification, not a rename-only fix.
- factEvidence.ts's `proseOf` helper — broadened to search `{sourceMaterial, projection}` combined rather than the old single `sourceProse`, since its callers (encounter-identity-retained, house-rule-governs-beside-source) are about CONTENT reaching the packet, not about which heading it lands under (that's covered directly by packetMessage.test.ts and M9 now).

M9 (measurements.ts): now checks both `sourceMaterial` and `projection` for a fact's typedPath/exactSubstring (search both halves, as instructed) — confirmed via the full discoveryProbes.test.ts suite (all M1-M9 probe executions still report m9.missing == []), including P8's typed path /data/mechanics/economies/use (projection) and P9's /data/armorClass/value, /data/hitPoints/value (source, unaffected).

shadow.ts's discovery-shadow-v2 admission check updated in place (no new schema version bump — PR #543 is still unmerged/pre-release, consistent with the existing "one v2 bump across .12.2/.12.3" decision) to check sourceMaterial/projection/residue instead of sourceProse.

Note: PROJECTION_CONTAINER_KEYS had to be a plain readonly array, not a `Set`, or discoveryOwnershipBoundary.test.ts's static analyzer flags it as a "module-scope-mutable-container" (it bans `new Set/Map` at module scope outright, to catch a jhpt rule/ruling cache — cannot distinguish that from a fixed lookup literal by syntax, so the array-literal form is the established accepted pattern per its own test fixture).

New evidence added to packetMessage.test.ts (5 cases): P4 fireball ability/damageOnSuccess move to projection while description+area stay source; P3 dragon actions[5].text/mechanics positional split; a null-valued projection leaf (magic-item:cube-of-force mechanics.ambiguities[0].canonicalResolution) stays projection; P10 (same governing record as P4, under a house rule) splits identically — reported since the review named P10 without specifying its fields; and a generic structural case walking every string-valued projection leaf of every retained P9 candidate (mixes rules-record and adventure-entity branches) asserting none of those exact pointer-qualified lines leak into that candidate's Source prose heading.
INTEGRATION REVIEW by Claude Captain at 029006a, merged into eshyra-o9bd.19.12.

The two containers added beyond the spec's named list (projection, useProfile) were INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, not accepted on report. Audit over all 108 distinct top-level data keys in the corpus for projection-marker fields (clauseId, readiness, economies, operations, damageOnSuccess, stateMachine) found exactly two undeclared hits: magic-item:crystal-ball and magic-item:ioun-stone 'variants'. Both are handled CORRECTLY by the recursive positional rule rather than needing declaration — variants[i] is {id,name,rarity,text,mechanics}, so variants[i].text classifies as source and variants[i].mechanics as projection, structurally identical to creature actions[i]. No leak. The added containers are accepted.

Corpus-wide behavioural audit run independently by the integrating agent over all 13 probe executions: 60 packet candidates, 851 source-side string leaves, ZERO paths under any projection container classified as source material, and ZERO such lines under the rendered '### Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)' heading. The reviewer's exact named case verified directly: spell:fireball mechanics.saves[0].ability='dexterity' and damageOnSuccess='half' are both in projection and absent from sourceMaterial, while 'a 20-foot-radius sphere' remains in sourceMaterial and absent from projection.

Verification at 029006a: npm run verify:worktree clean, 5341 passed / 20 skipped, no Biome warnings.
